items.q: I had met an English fellow at the Trois Mailletz named Ronald Sweetman... When Ron eventually returned to England he told me that he was going to try and get me over there... the dream of my friend Ronald Sweetman come true... visit for a few days our friends Ronald Sweetman and his wife Jennifer

ctx.x: In May 1965, I played there for a month and the boss asked me if it would be alright if he engaged the violinist Stuff Smith for 15 days to play as an added attraction with me and my group. Of course I agreed. I knew Stuff from way back and liked his hard swinging and groovy style. That man could swing like nobody else. Unfortunately he was in a bad state of health, suffering with stomach ulcers. He was not supposed to drink at all but couldn't help from having whiskey that he would dilute with plenty of water.…

My next thrill came in 1966 when I went to England for the first time to do a tour in that country. I had met an English fellow at the Trois Mailletz named Ronald Sweetman who was working in Paris and was a great jazz fan and record collector. He was also writing articles for different jazz magazines. When Ron eventually returned to England he told me that he was going to try and get me over there.

There was a regulation between the American Federation of musicians and the British musician's syndicate, whereby an American musician could play in England in exchange for an English one playing in the States.
